name: Hobbit
why_notable: Pseudonymous hacker who wrote netcat (nc) and announced it on the Bugtraq mailing list on 28 October 1995, with the final 1.10 release in March 1996. He designed it as a network version of the Unix cat command: a tool that moves raw bytes faithfully between a TCP or UDP socket and a pipe, scripts cleanly and keeps errors on stderr, which telnet did not. It became known as the 'TCP/IP Swiss army knife' and every later variant credits his code: OpenBSD's rewrite, Debian's netcat-traditional, GNU netcat, BusyBox nc and Nmap's Ncat. His source deliberately put the -e program-execution feature behind a compile flag named GAPING_SECURITY_HOLE. He is also known for the 1997 CIFS/SMB security analysis 'CIFS: Common Insecurities Fail Scrutiny'. His real name has never been made widely public.
